I'll suggest four games that can suck up a lot of time. Two are in the same genre but both are worth playing. In order of most time hovering:

  • Path of Exile
  • Dota 2
  • Grimdawn
  • Pillars of Eternity

Honestly, I'd say the time-sink value is a tie between Path of Exile and Dota 2 depending on your taste. Both have high bars for skill mastery and both are rewarding to play as you become increasingly better at them.

Dota 2 is directly competitive and is also team based, which some people find frustrating given the flux of online communities. But it's an incredibly addictive game and the steep learning curve (to mastery) invites you to play for huge chunks of time.

Like Dota 2, Path of Exile can eat up thousands of hours, but how you play and the strategies you choose are in your hands to a greater degree. Season play is definitely the way to go here, but also jump into Hardcore after you've got some experience with the game. So much fun and it has so many addictive qualities that it's difficult to not get hooked in.

Grimdawn follows suit to Path of Exile, but PoE's seasons and races both leave it as a more compelling long-term draw. Still, Grimdawn is an excellent way to spend three or four hundred hours with many of the same addictive notes as PoE. A true pleasure to play and conquer, several times.

Pillars of Eternity is the sort of game where you'll enjoy trying different strategies to replaying the content, but after three or four goes of that you'll start to feel burned out a bit. It will still provide a solid two hundred or more hours if you really dig its game play, more if you're a completionist and take on the core game and its two expansions.
